title: Rigveda 1.99: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.99: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.99 is a hymn of 1 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 68v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.99.1 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 7, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 68v
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>jā̱tave̍dase sunavāma̱ soma̍m arātīya̱to ni da̍hāti̱ veda̍ḥ | sa na̍ḥ parṣa̱d ati̍ du̱rgāṇi̱ viśvā̍ nā̱veva̱ sindhu̍ṁ duri̱tāty a̱gniḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>FOR Jâtavedas let us press the Soma: may he consume the wealth of the malignant. May Agni carry us through all our troubles, through grief as in a boat across the river.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 68v (OPenn image 70, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.97.4 ‹-śośucat agham›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 69r, begins in RV 1.100.1 ‹-havyaḥ bhareṣu marutvān naḥ›. Verse 1.99.1 ends on this page.
translation.edition_text: <sup>1</sup>jata-vedase | sunavāma | somam | arāti-yataḥ | ni | dahāti | vedaḥ | saḥ | naḥ | parṣat | ati | duḥ-gāni | viśvā | nāvāiva | sindhum | duḥ-itā | ati | agniḥ
